## Current Conditions (cont.)

### River Safety
- Drowning is the primary cause of death in the parks. View the rivers from a distance. The water is very cold and swift. Rocks near the river are slippery. The soil near and along the rivers can be unstable. It can collapse unexpectedly under the weight of people, including children, and result in falls into the river. Learn more about river safety

### Trails
- Check the Foothills Trails page for ideas to help you plan your trip.

### Roads
See the Road Conditions page for detailed information.

### Camping
- Potwisha Campground is open. Wood and charcoal fires are prohibited. Reservations are required. Visit recreation.gov to reserve your campsite.
- Buckeye Flat Campground is closed for 2026 due to damage from past winter storms.
- South Fork Campground is closed and not accessible due to damage from flooding and landslides from past winter storms. At this time, it is unknown when or if the campground will re-open.

### Free Ranger Programs
- A schedule of ranger-led programs is available on our events calendar . *Ranger programs are posted online at least one week in advance.
Giant Forest and Lodgepole Area Conditions (Sequoia National Park)

Página oficial NPS: Current Conditions — Sequoia & Kings Canyon National Parks
https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

## Current Conditions (cont.)

## Road Conditions and Closures
Check our road conditions page before you head into the parks. And we always recommend checking operating hours before arriving.
24-hour in-park road conditions: (559) 565-3341 (press 1, then 1 again).
For information about roads outside the park, visit the Caltrans website or call (800) 427-7623.

## Area Specific Conditions
Foothills Area Conditions (Sequoia National Park)

### Fire Restrictions
- Stage 1 fire restrictions are in effect. What this means:
- Wood and charcoal fires (including wood-burning stoves) are prohibited in all developed campgrounds below 3,000 feet (914 m) elevation (South Fork, Potwisha , and Buckeye Flat).
- Wood and charcoal fires (including wood-burning stoves) are prohibited in Hospital Rock picnic area and Ash Mountain picnic area next to Foothills Visitor Center .
- Smoking is prohibited below 6,000 feet (1829 m) elevation, except within an enclosed vehicle, a building in which smoking is allowed, a campground or picnic area where wood and charcoal fires are allowed, or a designated smoking area.
- Wood and charcoal fires (including wood-burning stoves) are prohibited below 6,000 feet (1829 m) elevation in backcountry undeveloped campsites.

### Weather
- Days are warm to hot and evenings and mornings are cool in the Foothills. Pack for a range of weather conditions when visiting. Dress appropriately and always bring plenty of water.

Página oficial NPS: Current Conditions — Sequoia & Kings Canyon National Parks
https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

### There are traffic delays and closures on Mineral King Road for the rest of the season. A schedule of traffic impacts are posted on our Road Construction page.

### Wilderness Permits
- Self-issue wilderness permits are available at the Mineral King Ranger Station.

### Facilities
- Some facilities may have limited hours.

### Campgrounds
- All campgrounds are reservation only. See the Campgrounds page for more details.

### Weather
- Between 7,500 to 14,000 feet elevation, Mineral King is characterized by mild daytime temperatures and cold nighttime and morning temperatures. Check weather forecasts .
Grant Grove Area Conditions (Kings Canyon National Park)

### Weather
- Check weather forecasts . Temperatures in the sequoia groves and the mountains are lower than California's Central Valley and the Sierra foothillls. Temperatures are cool in the mornings and evenings. Storms in the area can bring cold rain and some can produce wet snow. Bring extra layers of clothing to be prepared for all weather conditions. As always, make sure to protect yourself with sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water.

### Roads
- See the Road Conditions page.
- There are traffic delays of up to 30 minutes total on Generals Highway between Highway 180 and Giant Forest, including the Sherman Tree area.

## El clima manda aquí

Como en Kings Canyon, la altitud manda: en **Giant Forest** (~2,000 m) los veranos son templados (24-27°C) con noches frescas. Más abajo, en la entrada Ash Mountain, puede hacer más calor (32°C+).

En **invierno**, Giant Forest recibe nieve abundante — se requieren cadenas para subir. **Primavera y otoño** son el punto ideal: días de 18-22°C sin la multitud del verano.

## Air Quality
The dial below represents the current Air Quality Index (AQI) for the Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks' reporting area near the Foothills Visitor Center. Local conditions within the parks can vary to be worse or better than what is indicated. In summer months, ozone concentrations often exceed federal health standards. Ozone can have negative health effects. Learn more about air quality and how it can impact your trip.
Note: This is an old image from the webcam that may not represent the current conditions in the park. For an updated view of the Giant Forest, please click the link in the text about the webcam.
Sequoia National Park Webcam
The Giant Forest webcam looks west from the edge of the Giant Forest. In summer, a gray layer of polluted air can be seen forming over the valley. Rarely can you see both the San Joaquin Valley and the Coast Range beyond that. With increasing air pollution blowing up into the Sierra Nevada from the Bay Area and the Valley, very clear days are becoming ever more rare.

### Trails
- Trails within the Grant Grove area are open. Check at the Kings Canyon Visitor Center for the most up-to-date trail conditions.
- Only 2.5 miles of trails in the Redwood Canyon area are maintained. Traveling on unmaintained trails is not advised due to tree hazards following damage from the 2021 KNP Complex Fire.

### Camping
- All camping is by reservation only, through recreation.gov .
- Azalea Campground is open. During spring, summer, and fall, camping is by reservation only. During the winter, part of the campground is open on a first-come, first-served basis.
- Crystal Springs Campground is closed for the season.
- Sunset Campground is closed for the season.
- During the spring, summer, and fall, most campgrounds fill well in advance of weekends and holidays. Reservation windows vary between campgrounds, see each individual campground page or recreation.gov for more information.

## Current Conditions

## Alerts
Lower elevations are usually sunny and hot while higher elevations can be cool in mornings and evenings. Prepare for both before you visit the parks!
NPS Photo / Rebecca Stievater

## Autumn in the Sequoia Groves
If you plan to visit the sequoias, be prepared for pleasantly warm daytime temperatures and cool conditions in the mornings and evenings. Bring clothing for both warm and cold weather.
The lower-elevation foothills can still be very warm during the day. Some campgrounds are still open and camping is by reservation only. There are traffic delays on Generals Highway between Giant Forest and Highway 180.
To stay updated on the many changes occurring during this period of transition, read through our tips and tricks below!

### Weather
Check the weather forecast before you head out! Autumn is a wonderful time to visit giant sequoias, but only when you are prepared for the conditions. Plan ahead by packing multiple layers of clothing so that you can adjust to warmer or cooler conditions.

## Half Dome Cables
The most famous—or infamous—part of the hike is the ascent up the cables. The two metal cables allow hikers to climb the last 400 feet to the summit without rock climbing equipment. Since 1919, relatively few people have fallen and died on the cables. However, injuries are not uncommon for those acting irresponsibly.
The Half Dome cables usually go back up the Friday before the last Monday in May (Memorial Day) and come down the day after the second Monday in October . These dates are subject to change based on conditions.

### Tips while using the cables:
- Take your time and be patient with slower hikers
- Allow faster hikers to pass you (when possible)
- Remain on the inside of the cables

### Do not attempt the ascent if:
- Storm clouds are in the area
- The ground is wet. Nearly all fatal falls from the cables have happened when the rock was wet, which make the rock (and cables) very slick
- The cables are down for the winter (typically, from the day after Columbus Day until Memorial Day weekend) (check conditions update for status and any available updates)

Parque: Parque Nacional Yosemite — Sección: faqs

P: ¿Cuánto cuesta entrar?
R: 35 USD por vehículo (7 días). Verifica en nps.gov/yose — puede haber surcharge a no residentes.

P: ¿Necesito reservar para entrar en carro?
R: De mayo a septiembre sí: necesitas reservación de día específico (recreation.gov). Se abren 2 semanas antes y en cupos especiales con más antelación. Fuera de temporada no se requiere.

P: ¿Qué pasa si no consigo reservación de carro?
R: Puedes entrar en transporte público (tren AMTRAK + autobús YARTS desde Merced o Fresno) sin necesidad de reservación. Muchos lo prefieren porque evitas el estrés del tráfico.

P: ¿Cuándo hay menos gente?
R: Noviembre a marzo. Hay nieve y algunas instalaciones cierran, pero el parque es precioso y sin multitudes. Abril también es bueno con las cascadas en su máximo.

P: ¿Cuántos días necesito?
R: 3-4 días para ver lo principal del valle. Con 2 días puedes hacer El Capitan, Yosemite Falls y el espejo de Half Dome, pero es apresurado.

P: ¿El Half Dome requiere permiso especial?
R: Sí, el tramo final con cables (cables route) requiere permiso por lotería, muy competido. Si no lo consigues, la vista desde Mirror Lake o Valley View es igualmente espectacular.

P: ¿Hay señal de celular?
R: Casi nula en el Valle. Descarga tu mapa y las reservaciones antes de entrar.

Parque: Parque Nacional Yosemite — Sección: common_fears

P: ¿Necesito ser montañista o estar en forma?
R: No para el Valle, que es plano y tiene shuttle. Las vistas más famosas están a corta caminata. La parte exigente (alto país, Half Dome) es opcional y para después. Para tu primera vez, quédate en el Valle.

P: ¿Qué hago si me encuentro con un oso?
R: Mantén la calma, haz ruido y retrocede lentamente sin darle la espalda.

P: ¿Es cierto que se necesita reservación para entrar?
R: En temporada alta, algunos años sí. Revisa las fechas en nps.gov antes de ir y, si aplica, reserva tu entrada con tiempo. Fuera de temporada alta no suele pedirse.

P: ¿Puedo subir Half Dome en mi primera visita?
R: Mejor no. Requiere permiso por lotería, se sube por cables sobre roca expuesta y ha habido accidentes mortales. No es una caminata para principiantes. Hay muchísimo que ver en el Valle sin ese riesgo.

P: Está lejos, ¿vale la pena el viaje?
R: Son 5 a 7 horas desde el sur de California, sí. Pero es uno de los parques más impresionantes del mundo y el Valle es fácil de disfrutar. Ve en primavera por las cascadas o en otoño por la calma y lo vas a recordar toda la vida.

Página oficial NPS: Half Dome Day Hike — Yosemite National Park
https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/halfdome.htm

## Safety

### Weather
The summit of Half Dome is a dangerous place during a lightning storm. Check the weather forecast before your hike and try to reach the summit early in the day to avoid thunderstorms, which are more common in the afternoon (but can occur at any time). If a storm appears nearby, do not continue to the summit and, if in the summit area, leave the area (while still using caution when descending the cables and steps).

## Half Dome Cables
The most famous—or infamous—part of the hike is the ascent up the cables. The two metal cables allow hikers to climb the last 400 feet to the summit without rock climbing equipment. Since 1919, relatively few people have fallen and died on the cables. However, injuries are not uncommon for those acting irresponsibly.
The Half Dome cables usually go back up the Friday before the last Monday in May (Memorial Day) and come down the day after the second Monday in October . These dates are subject to change based on conditions.

### Tips while using the cables:
- Take your time and be patient with slower hikers
- Allow faster hikers to pass you (when possible)
- Remain on the inside of the cables

### Do not attempt the ascent if:
- Storm clouds are in the area
- The ground is wet. Nearly all fatal falls from the cables have happened when the rock was wet, which make the rock (and cables) very slick
- The cables are down for the winter (typically, from the day after Columbus Day until Memorial Day weekend) (check conditions update for status and any available updates)

P: ¿Necesito ser montañista o estar en forma?
R: No para el Valle, que es plano y tiene shuttle. Las vistas más famosas están a corta caminata. La parte exigente (alto país, Half Dome) es opcional y para después. Para tu primera vez, quédate en el Valle.

P: ¿Qué hago si me encuentro con un oso?
R: Mantén la calma, haz ruido y retrocede lentamente sin darle la espalda.

P: ¿Es cierto que se necesita reservación para entrar?
R: En temporada alta, algunos años sí. Revisa las fechas en nps.gov antes de ir y, si aplica, reserva tu entrada con tiempo. Fuera de temporada alta no suele pedirse.

P: ¿Puedo subir Half Dome en mi primera visita?
R: Mejor no. Requiere permiso por lotería, se sube por cables sobre roca expuesta y ha habido accidentes mortales. No es una caminata para principiantes. Hay muchísimo que ver en el Valle sin ese riesgo.

P: Está lejos, ¿vale la pena el viaje?
R: Son 5 a 7 horas desde el sur de California, sí. Pero es uno de los parques más impresionantes del mundo y el Valle es fácil de disfrutar. Ve en primavera por las cascadas o en otoño por la calma y lo vas a recordar toda la vida.

## Preparation (cont.)

### Water
One of the easiest ways to ensure a safe, enjoyable hike is to be sure to have plenty of water. Weather conditions and personal preference affect the amount of water you need, but suggested minimum amounts per person are:
1 gallon (4 liters) if hiking to the top of Half Dome
2 quarts (2 liters) if hiking only to the top of Nevada Fall
1 quart (1 liter) if hiking only to the top of Vernal Fall
The only treated water on the trail is available (summer only) at a drinking fountain at the Vernal Fall Footbridge (less than a mile from the trailhead). Merced River water is available up to Little Yosemite Valley, however you should treat this water by boiling, using iodine, or using a giardia-rated water filter. Drinking untreated river water may cause significant illness.

### Restrooms
Flush toilets are available at the Vernal Fall Footbridge (below Vernal Fall). Composting toilets are available near Emerald Pool (above Vernal Fall), near the top of Nevada Fall, and in Little Yosemite Valley.
At any other location, you are required to bury any solid human waste at least six inches (15 cm) deep and at least 100 feet (30 m) from water or trails. Pack out toilet paper.

Length: 7 miles (11.3 km) out and back round trip

Difficulty: Moderate *

Texto oficial NPS (inglés): “One of the easiest ways to ensure a safe, enjoyable hike is to be sure to have plenty of water. Weather conditions and personal preference affect the amount of water you need, but suggested minimum amounts per person are: 1 gallon (4 liters) if hiking to the top of Half Dome; 2 quarts (2 liters) if hiking only to the top of Nevada Fall; 1 quart (1 liter) if hiking only to the top of Vernal Fall.”

Parque: Parque Nacional Yellowstone — Sección: wildlife

Bisontes (los verás garantizado), alces, osos negros y grizzly, lobos (Lamar Valley), berrendos y águilas. Mínimo 23 m de distancia de bisontes/alces y 91 m de osos y lobos — es regla, no sugerencia.

Parque: Parque Nacional y Reserva Katmai — Sección: safety

## Seguridad real (no para asustarte, para que regreses bien)

- **Escuela de osos — obligatoria al aterrizar.** Cero comida fuera de las zonas selladas (ni un chicle en el bolsillo).
- **50 m de distancia mínima**, y prioridad de paso absoluta — si un oso va por la pasarela, tú esperas.
- **En la práctica**, los guardaparques orquestan todo — es de las formas más seguras del planeta de estar cerca de osos salvajes.

Página oficial NPS: Bears and Food Storage — Yosemite National Park
https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/bears.htm

## How to Store Your Food (cont.)

### Picnicking and Hiking
Always keep your food within arm's reach and don't turn your back to your food; never leave food unattended. Bears may investigate picnic areas or backpacks for food even in your presence, so be alert.

### Backpacking in the Wilderness
Bear resistant food containers ("bear canisters") are required for overnight hikers throughout the wilderness (counterbalance food hangs are no longer legal). In Yosemite and the southern Sierra, bear canisters are the only effective and proven method of preventing bears from getting human food.

## Bear Encounters
If you see a bear outside of developed areas, keep your distance: Remain at least 50 yards (four shuttle bus lengths).
If you see a bear in a developed area or if a bear approaches you, scare it away by yelling very loudly and aggressively.
Find out more about what to do if you see a bear .

Parque: Parque Nacional Shenandoah — Sección: common_fears

P: ¿Y si se me cruza un oso?
R: Las reglas son simples: mantén distancia, haz ruido al caminar para no sorprenderlos y guarda bien tu comida. Si ves uno, retrocede lentamente sin darle la espalda.

P: ¿La carretera Skyline Drive es peligrosa?
R: No, es una carretera panorámica pavimentada y en excelente estado. Solo debes respetar el límite de 35 mph, porque los osos y venados cruzan sin avisar.

Parque: Parque Nacional Yosemite — Sección: wildlife

Osos negros (guarda la comida en los casilleros, son listísimos), venados, coyotes, marmotas y el pika en las alturas. Ver un oso de lejos es emocionante; alimentarlo lo condena a muerte — nunca lo hagas.

Parque: Parque Nacional Yosemite — Sección: safety

## Seguridad real (no para asustarte, para que regreses bien)

- **Osos — muy activos.** Guarda TODA la comida en los casilleros de metal — los osos han aprendido a abrir carros. Una multa por comida en el carro puede superar $100.
- **Cascadas y bordes.** Las rocas cerca de las cascadas son extremadamente resbaladizas. Cada año hay caídas fatales — no te acerques al borde aunque parezca seguro.
- **Reservación.** En verano puede requerir reservación de entrada — verifica en recreation.gov antes de salir.
- **Agua.** Lleva **2 litros por persona** aunque solo vayas a los miradores del Valle.

Parque: Parque Nacional Sequoia — Sección: safety

## Seguridad real (no para asustarte, para que regreses bien)

- **Osos negros — guarda TODA la comida.** Esto es territorio de osos. La comida y cualquier cosa con olor (hasta pasta de dientes) va en los **casilleros metálicos**, **nunca a la vista dentro del carro**. Los guardias lo revisan. Si ves un oso: *no corras*, haz ruido y retrocede despacio.
- **La carretera de montaña.** La Generals Highway es **empinada y con curvas cerradas**. Maneja despacio, no te pegues al de adelante y usa **marcha baja en las bajadas** para no quemar los frenos. En invierno, **cadenas**.
- **La altura.** Giant Forest está a ~2,000 m. El sendero al General Sherman *regresa cuesta arriba* — tómalo con calma e hidrátate.
- **Sin señal.** No hay celular en casi todo el parque: **descarga tu mapa offline** y dile a alguien tu plan.
- **Clima de montaña.** Cambia rápido. Lleva capas y revisa el pronóstico.

Parque: Parque Nacional Yellowstone — Sección: safety

## Seguridad real (no para asustarte, para que regreses bien)

- **Zonas geotérmicas — no te salgas del sendero.** El suelo puede ser una costra delgada sobre agua hirviendo. Cada año hay accidentes graves por salirse de las pasarelas.
- **Bisontes.** Son el animal más peligroso del parque — más rápidos de lo que parecen. Mantén mínimo 25 metros siempre.
- **Osos.** Lleva **spray anti-osos** en los senderos. Guarda toda la comida en los casilleros — nunca en el carro.
- **Frío nocturno.** Hiela de noche incluso en verano. Lleva capas aunque salga sol.

Parque: Parque Nacional Yosemite — Sección: campgrounds

• Upper Pines Campground (recomendado): $26/noche. Reserva 5 meses antes, el día 15 de cada mes a las 7am hora Pacífico. ⚠️ VERIFICAR (IA) precio vigente., RV máx 35 ft, señal: Débil (fondo de valle) — Nuestra base para principiantes en Yosemite: el único campground del Valle abierto todo el año, a pasos del shuttle gratuito y de Half Dome Village (duchas de paga, tienda, restaurantes). Se llena en minutos cuando abre la reserva 5 meses antes — ten tu cuenta de recreation.gov lista desde antes.
• North Pines Campground: $26/noche aprox. ⚠️ VERIFICAR (IA) precio vigente en recreation.gov., RV máx 40 ft, señal: Débil — Junto al río Merced y el arroyo Tenaya — de los más pedidos por su ambiente junto al agua. Solo abre marzo-octubre. Acepta RV hasta 40 ft, más grande que Upper Pines.
• Camp 4: $10 por persona por noche. Lotería diaria en temporada alta — sistema distinto al resto de campgrounds. ⚠️ VERIFICAR (IA) mecanismo vigente., señal: Débil — El campground histórico de escaladores, cultura propia desde los años 60. Solo tiendas, sin RV. En temporada alta funciona por lotería diaria, no reserva anticipada — hay que presentarse en persona muy temprano.

Página oficial NPS: Current Conditions — Yosemite National Park
https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

## Current Conditions (cont.)

## Campground Information
Camping and sleeping in a vehicle is only allowed in campsites you are registered to stay in. If campgrounds are full, you must find a campground elsewhere to stay in. If all open campgrounds in the park are full, you must leave the park to camp or sleep in your vehicle.

### Yosemite Valley:
Open: Reservation required: Upper Pines, Lower Pines, North Pines, Camp 4
First-come, first-served: None
Closed: None

### Outside Yosemite Valley:
Open: Reservation required: Wawona, Hodgdon Meadow, Crane Flat (closes Oct 12), Tamarack Flat (closes Oct 12), Porcupine Flat (closes Oct 11)
First-come, first-served : None
Closed: Bridalveil Creek, White Wolf, Yosemite Creek, Tuolumne Meadows
View estimated opening and closing dates in 2026 for all campgrounds.
Reservations are available up to five months in advance and are strongly recommended. If you don't have a reservation, get details about camping without a reservation .
Visit Yosemite Hospitality's website for lodging information (including information about Housekeeping Camp and High Sierra Camps). Reservations are available and recommended up to 366 days in advance.

Parque: Parque Nacional Yosemite — Sección: faqs

P: ¿Cuánto cuesta entrar?
R: 35 USD por vehículo (7 días). Verifica en nps.gov/yose — puede haber surcharge a no residentes.

P: ¿Necesito reservar para entrar en carro?
R: De mayo a septiembre sí: necesitas reservación de día específico (recreation.gov). Se abren 2 semanas antes y en cupos especiales con más antelación. Fuera de temporada no se requiere.

P: ¿Qué pasa si no consigo reservación de carro?
R: Puedes entrar en transporte público (tren AMTRAK + autobús YARTS desde Merced o Fresno) sin necesidad de reservación. Muchos lo prefieren porque evitas el estrés del tráfico.

P: ¿Cuándo hay menos gente?
R: Noviembre a marzo. Hay nieve y algunas instalaciones cierran, pero el parque es precioso y sin multitudes. Abril también es bueno con las cascadas en su máximo.

P: ¿Cuántos días necesito?
R: 3-4 días para ver lo principal del valle. Con 2 días puedes hacer El Capitan, Yosemite Falls y el espejo de Half Dome, pero es apresurado.

P: ¿El Half Dome requiere permiso especial?
R: Sí, el tramo final con cables (cables route) requiere permiso por lotería, muy competido. Si no lo consigues, la vista desde Mirror Lake o Valley View es igualmente espectacular.

P: ¿Hay señal de celular?
R: Casi nula en el Valle. Descarga tu mapa y las reservaciones antes de entrar.

https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/camping.htm

## Campground Reservations

### Camping in Yosemite
Making a Reservation
Campground Reservation FAQ
Camping Without a Reservation
Campgrounds
Camping Regulations
Yosemite National Park has 13 popular campgrounds , all of which are on a reservation system from April through October. During winter, Camp 4, Wawona, and Hodgdon Meadow are first-come, first-served campgrounds , but can fill during holidays and weekends.
Reservations are available at different times depending on the campground. All non-lottery reservations are released at 7 am Pacific time and sell out within minutes.
For your best chance of getting a reservation, be sure your clock is set accurately. Log in and be ready to go at Recreation.gov before 7 am Pacific time. You can find more help making reservations and other frequently asked questions .

## When to Make a Reservation
Only Upper Pines Campground is on reservations all year. View opening dates and reservation seasons for all campgrounds.

### Five Months in Advance
Reservations for these campgrounds are released five months in advance on the 15th of each month.
- Upper Pines (open all year)
- Lower Pines (open sometime in April to sometime in October)
- North Pines (open sometime in April to sometime in October)
- Wawona (open all year; reservation required from sometime in April to sometime in October)
- Hodgdon Meadow (open all year; reservation required from sometime in April to sometime in October)
View this year's opening and closing dates .

Parque: Parque Nacional Yosemite — Sección: basecamp

El Valle mismo (si consigues reserva) o Mariposa/Oakhurst como alternativa a 45 min-1 h.

Parque: Parque Nacional Yosemite — Sección: preparation

Para Yosemite Valley no necesitas condición especial; sí necesitas planear con tiempo, porque se llena.

Antes de ir: revisa si hay reservación de entrada para tus fechas y resérvala. Reserva hospedaje con meses de anticipación (o duerme en un pueblo de entrada). Llega con el tanque lleno.

En el parque: usa el shuttle gratuito del Valle y camina los senderos fáciles. Si vas por las cascadas, ve en primavera (mayo-junio). Guarda la comida en los casilleros para osos.

## Plan de Preparación
1. Temporada: primavera para cascadas, otoño para menos gente.
2. Reservación de entrada: confírmala y resérvala si aplica.
3. Hospedaje reservado con tiempo (o pueblo cercano).
4. Tanque lleno antes de subir.
5. Capas de ropa: el clima de montaña cambia.
6. Comida en casilleros para osos; nunca en el auto a la vista.
7. Quédate en el Valle para tu primera vez; deja Half Dome para después (o nunca, no pasa nada).

Página oficial NPS: Campground Reservations — Yosemite National Park
https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/camping.htm

## Campground Reservations (cont.)

### Two Months in Advance
Half of the campsites at Tuolumne Meadows Campground are released two months in advance on the 15th of each month. (The other half are released on a rolling daily window two weeks in advance.)
This campground is open from approximately July to late September. View this year's opening and closing dates .

### Two Weeks in Advance
Reservations for these campgrounds are released two weeks in advance on a rolling daily window (i.e., 14 days in advance of arrival date):
- Bridalveil Creek (open sometime in July to early September)
- Crane Flat (open July to early October)
- Tamarack Flat (open July to early October)
- White Wolf (open July to early September)
- Yosemite Creek (open July to early September)
- Porcupine Flat (open July to early October)
- half of Tuolumne Meadows (open July to late September)
View this year's opening and closing dates .

### One Week in Advance
Camp 4 reservations are released one week in advance on a rolling daily window (i.e., 7 days in advance of arrival date). Reservations required April 18 through October 31, 2025 (returning to first-come, first-served November 1).

5. Capas de ropa: el clima de montaña cambia.
6. Comida en casilleros para osos; nunca en el auto a la vista.
7. Quédate en el Valle para tu primera vez; deja Half Dome para después (o nunca, no pasa nada).

Yosemite National Park has 13 popular campgrounds , all of which are on a reservation system from April through October. During winter, Camp 4, Wawona, and Hodgdon Meadow are first-come, first-served campgrounds , but can fill during holidays and weekends.
Reservations are available at different times depending on the campground. All non-lottery reservations are released at 7 am Pacific time and sell out within minutes.
For your best chance of getting a reservation, be sure your clock is set accurately. Log in and be ready to go at Recreation.gov before 7 am Pacific time. You can find more help making reservations and other frequently asked questions .

## When to Make a Reservation
Only Upper Pines Campground is on reservations all year. View opening dates and reservation seasons for all campgrounds.

### Five Months in Advance
Reservations for these campgrounds are released five months in advance on the 15th of each month.
- Upper Pines (open all year)
- Lower Pines (open sometime in April to sometime in October)
- North Pines (open sometime in April to sometime in October)
- Wawona (open all year; reservation required from sometime in April to sometime in October)
- Hodgdon Meadow (open all year; reservation required from sometime in April to sometime in October)

Parque: Parque Nacional Yosemite — Sección: common_fears

P: ¿Necesito ser montañista o estar en forma?
R: No para el Valle, que es plano y tiene shuttle. Las vistas más famosas están a corta caminata. La parte exigente (alto país, Half Dome) es opcional y para después. Para tu primera vez, quédate en el Valle.

P: ¿Qué hago si me encuentro con un oso?
R: Mantén la calma, haz ruido y retrocede lentamente sin darle la espalda.

P: ¿Es cierto que se necesita reservación para entrar?
R: En temporada alta, algunos años sí. Revisa las fechas en nps.gov antes de ir y, si aplica, reserva tu entrada con tiempo. Fuera de temporada alta no suele pedirse.

P: ¿Puedo subir Half Dome en mi primera visita?
R: Mejor no. Requiere permiso por lotería, se sube por cables sobre roca expuesta y ha habido accidentes mortales. No es una caminata para principiantes. Hay muchísimo que ver en el Valle sin ese riesgo.

P: Está lejos, ¿vale la pena el viaje?
R: Son 5 a 7 horas desde el sur de California, sí. Pero es uno de los parques más impresionantes del mundo y el Valle es fácil de disfrutar. Ve en primavera por las cascadas o en otoño por la calma y lo vas a recordar toda la vida.

Parque: Parque Nacional Yosemite — Sección: faqs

P: ¿Cuánto cuesta entrar?
R: 35 USD por vehículo (7 días). Verifica en nps.gov/yose — puede haber surcharge a no residentes.

P: ¿Necesito reservar para entrar en carro?
R: De mayo a septiembre sí: necesitas reservación de día específico (recreation.gov). Se abren 2 semanas antes y en cupos especiales con más antelación. Fuera de temporada no se requiere.

P: ¿Qué pasa si no consigo reservación de carro?
R: Puedes entrar en transporte público (tren AMTRAK + autobús YARTS desde Merced o Fresno) sin necesidad de reservación. Muchos lo prefieren porque evitas el estrés del tráfico.

P: ¿Cuándo hay menos gente?
R: Noviembre a marzo. Hay nieve y algunas instalaciones cierran, pero el parque es precioso y sin multitudes. Abril también es bueno con las cascadas en su máximo.

P: ¿Cuántos días necesito?
R: 3-4 días para ver lo principal del valle. Con 2 días puedes hacer El Capitan, Yosemite Falls y el espejo de Half Dome, pero es apresurado.

P: ¿El Half Dome requiere permiso especial?
R: Sí, el tramo final con cables (cables route) requiere permiso por lotería, muy competido. Si no lo consigues, la vista desde Mirror Lake o Valley View es igualmente espectacular.

P: ¿Hay señal de celular?
R: Casi nula en el Valle. Descarga tu mapa y las reservaciones antes de entrar.

Parque: Parque Nacional Yosemite — Sección: why_visit

Yosemite es de esos lugares que ves en foto toda la vida y crees que exageran — hasta que estás parado frente a El Capitan o ves caer Yosemite Falls. No exageran.

Y aunque parece un parque de montañistas, no lo es para empezar: casi toda la postal está en Yosemite Valley, un valle plano que recorres a pie o en shuttle gratis. Puedes vivir lo más impresionante del parque sin una caminata difícil.

Seamos honestos: recibe muchísima gente en verano y a veces pide reservación de entrada. Pero si vas en primavera por las cascadas, o en otoño por la calma, y te quedas en el Valle, es probablemente la mejor primera gran salida a la naturaleza que puedes hacer en California.

Reserva 5 meses antes, el día 15 de cada mes a las 7am hora Pacífico. ⚠️ VERIFICAR (IA) precio vigente., RV máx 35 ft, señal: Débil (fondo de valle) — Nuestra base para principiantes en Yosemite: el único campground del Valle abierto todo el año, a pasos del shuttle gratuito y de Half Dome Village (duchas de paga, tienda, restaurantes). Se llena en minutos cuando abre la reserva 5 meses antes — ten tu cuenta de recreation.gov lista desde antes.
• North Pines Campground: $26/noche aprox. ⚠️ VERIFICAR (IA) precio vigente en recreation.gov., RV máx 40 ft, señal: Débil — Junto al río Merced y el arroyo Tenaya — de los más pedidos por su ambiente junto al agua. Solo abre marzo-octubre. Acepta RV hasta 40 ft, más grande que Upper Pines.
• Camp 4: $10 por persona por noche. Lotería diaria en temporada alta — sistema distinto al resto de campgrounds. ⚠️ VERIFICAR (IA) mecanismo vigente., señal: Débil — El campground histórico de escaladores, cultura propia desde los años 60. Solo tiendas, sin RV. En temporada alta funciona por lotería diaria, no reserva anticipada — hay que presentarse en persona muy temprano.

### Current Roadwork
El Capitan Bridge Stabilization Project
Stabilization work on El Capitan Bridge (which goes over the Merced River near El Capitan Meadow) will result in 15-minute delays, Monday through Friday, 7 am to 7 pm, through December 2026. Some brief closures are also possible (detour available).
Big Oak Flat Road Fire Safety Work (15-minute delays)
Expect 15-minute delays on weekdays. This work will help restore more resilient forest conditions and safely reintroduce fire by conducting mechanical vegetation reduction work along Big Oak Flat Road between Foresta and Big Oak Flat. Crews are removing dead and fallen wood and reducing smaller trees near the road. This work reduces wildfire risk to visitors, infrastructure, and firefighters, and helps prepare the area for future prescribed fire or to better withstand unplanned wildfires.

### Overnight guest lodging closure in effect
- Effective Monday, August 31, 2026, all park concessions will halt overnight accommodations . This includes hotel facilities operated by Xanterra, such as El Tovar, Bright Angel Lodge, Maswik Lodge, and Phantom Ranch, as well as Delaware North’s Yavapai Lodge and Trailer Village. Overnight hotel accommodations located outside the park in the town of Tusayan will not be impacted by changes in park operations.
- This action was taken because a flash flood on August 29, caused extensive damage to infrastructure in the inner canyon, including the Transcanyon Waterline, which supplies water from the canyon for use in the park. The waterline is currently not operational, leaving the park with limited water reserves and requiring significant water conservation measures to ensure available supplies can be maintained. ## Grand Canyon National Park Announces Projected Dates for Restoring Water to South Rim
September 2026 sunrise from Maricopa Point
NPS/J. Baird
News Release Date: September 19, 2026
Contact:
Grand Canyon Office of Communications
Grand Canyon National Park today announced tentative dates for the restoration of water services to the South Rim residences and concessionaires within the park.
Based upon construction timetables, the National Park Service Incident Management Team projects the park will be able to start pumping water by Nov. 16 from the Bright Angel Creek intake to the new water treatment plan. The National Park Service estimates distribution from the new treatment plant to residents will begin by Thanksgiving, allowing concessionaires to begin a phased approach to providing services to overnight guests at that time. These dates are tentative and residents and concessionaires will be notified as construction is completed.
The park is working on an agreement to haul about 200,000 gallons of water per day to replenish the water storage tanks. If finalized, this agreement would stabilize the tank levels and enable the park to maintain operations through the projected date to start pumping, assuming the current water usage of about 137,000 gallons per day stays steady.
Once the pumps start drawing water from the Bright Angel Creek, it will take about 45 days to fully fill the tanks.

## Phantom Ranch
Visit our Key Hiking Messages webpage for current trail closures near Phantom Ranch.
CLOSED — As of August 29, 2026, due to flash flooding:
The entirety of Phantom Ranch , including Bright Angel Campground , the Phantom Ranch Canteen , and Phantom Ranch cabins . The Black Bridge and Silver Bridge spanning the Colorado River.
The entirety of the North Kaibab Trail. This includes the North Kaibab Trailhead to Phantom Ranch . This closure is a result of significant flash flooding to the Bright Angel Canyon on 8/29.
There is no estimated reopening of these closure areas at this time.
Phantom Ranch, at the bottom of the Grand Canyon, is a popular destination for both hikers and mule riders. Overnight dormitories and cabins can be reserved and meals are available for purchase. Advance reservations for meals and lodging are required.
Phantom Ranch Reservations are made through Grand Canyon National Park Lodges (Xanterra Parks and Resorts) via an on-line lottery 15 months in advance.
( An NPS backcountry camping permit is not required for overnight stays in Phantom Ranch accomodations.) The park's Backcountry Information Center does not make reservations for Phantom Ranch lodging or meals. Reservations are made through Grand Canyon National Park Lodges.
Reservations for the nearby Bright Angel Campground (NPS) are made through the park's Backcountry Information Center.

• New River Gorge Bridge (mirador) (mejor momento: Atardecer) [38.0678, -81.0778] — El puente de acero de un solo arco más largo del hemisferio occidental, mirador en Canyon Rim.

• Long Point Trail (5.1km, 2h), 80m desnivel — El sendero estrella: bosque plano y al final, la vista frontal del puente sobre el cañón. La foto del parque se gana aquí. Apto principiante: sí
• Canyon Rim Boardwalk (0.5km, 0.5h), 40m desnivel — Pasarela del centro de visitantes a dos miradores del puente. El tramo superior es accesible; el inferior baja 178 escalones (y los subes de regreso). Apto principiante: sí
• Endless Wall Trail (7.8km, 3h), 90m desnivel — Bosque de rododendros por el borde del acantilado con miradores al cañón (Diamond Point es el premio). Cuidado con los bordes sin barandal. Apto principiante: sí
• Sandstone Falls Boardwalk (0.8km, 0.5h), 5m desnivel — Pasarelas accesibles sobre las cascadas más anchas del New River, en el lado sur del parque. Ideal con niños y abuelos. Apto principiante: sí
• Kaymoor Miners Trail (3.2km, 2.5h), 300m desnivel — Baja 821 escalones a las ruinas de la mina de carbón en el fondo del cañón. La historia es fascinante; la subida de regreso, un entrenamiento completo. Apto principiante: no

## Seguridad real (no para asustarte, para que regreses bien)

- **Angels Landing — solo si tienes experiencia.** Tiene cadenas y bordes de 450 m de caída. No es para principiantes ni para quien le tema a las alturas — es opcional y el parque es increíble sin hacerlo.
- **Inundaciones repentinas en los cañones.** Si llueve en cualquier lugar de la cuenca, The Narrows puede inundarse en minutos. Verifica el pronóstico antes de entrar al cañón.
- **Calor en el cañón.** En verano el cañón concentra el calor. Lleva **2-3 litros de agua** y camina temprano.
- **Shuttle.** En temporada alta es obligatorio — llega temprano porque se satura.

Parque: Parque Nacional Yellowstone — Sección: hikes

• Pasarelas de Upper Geyser Basin (Old Faithful) (2.4km, 1.5h), 10m desnivel — Red de pasarelas planas entre la mayor concentración de géiseres del mundo. Camina lo que quieras y regresa para la erupción de Old Faithful. Apto principiante: sí
• Mirador de Grand Prismatic (Fairy Falls Trail) (2.6km, 1h), 60m desnivel — Caminata plana hasta el mirador elevado de la fuente termal de colores. La foto que viniste a buscar se gana aquí, no abajo. Apto principiante: sí
• Brink of the Lower Falls (1.2km, 1h), 180m desnivel — Bajada corta pero empinada al borde mismo de la cascada de 94 m. La subida de regreso cuesta: tómala con calma. Apto principiante: sí
• Mystic Falls (3.9km, 2h), 150m desnivel — Sendero de bosque desde Biscuit Basin a una cascada de 21 m. Tranquilo y con poca gente. Lleva spray para osos. Apto principiante: sí
• Pasarelas de Mammoth Hot Springs (2.8km, 1.5h), 90m desnivel — Terrazas de travertino blanco que parecen de otro planeta. Recorre las terrazas bajas si prefieres menos subida. Apto principiante: sí

Parque: Parque Nacional Zion — Sección: common_fears

P: ¿Es muy difícil para alguien sin experiencia?
R: No. Hay paseos planos junto al río perfectos para empezar (Riverside Walk, Pa'rus). Los retos legendarios como Angels Landing son 100% opcionales — el parque es espectacular sin ellos.

P: ¿Tengo que hacer Angels Landing o The Narrows?
R: Para nada, y es bueno saberlo. Angels Landing tiene cadenas y caídas mortales; The Narrows es caminar dentro del río. Son opcionales y para gente con experiencia. Te pierdes cero de la belleza de Zion si los saltas.

P: ¿Cómo funciona el shuttle obligatorio?
R: En temporada alta no puedes manejar dentro del cañón: usas el shuttle gratuito que para en cada sendero. Llega temprano (antes de las 9 a.m.) porque se satura. Es fácil una vez que entiendes el sistema.

P: ¿Necesito reservar algo?
R: Para entrar, no. Pero si quieres hacer Angels Landing necesitas un permiso por sorteo (recreation.gov). Para todo lo demás, solo llega temprano por el shuttle.

## Nonresident Fees (cont.)

## If a nonresident has a valid Annual Pass purchased in 2025, will it cover entrance fees and nonresident fees?
Yes, older passes will be honored with the original terms of the pass. A valid Annual Pass purchased before January 1, 2026, is valid for 12 months from the time of purchase and will cover park entrance fees and nonresident fees for the pass holder and anyone traveling with them in a private vehicle or on two motorcycles, or for the pass holder and three additional adults where fees are charged per person.

## Will nonresidents traveling with a pass holder carrying any America the Beautiful Pass or park-specific annual pass need to pay entrance fees and nonresident fees?
Regardless of the year issued, all valid America the Beautiful Passes and park-specific annual passes will cover entrance fees and nonresident fees for the pass holder and passengers in a private vehicle or on two motorcycles. At sites that charge per person, all valid America the Beautiful Passes and park-specific annual passes will cover entrance fees and nonresident fees for the pass holder and three additional adults.

## How will fee free days work?
Fee free days generally allow free entrance to all park visitors. Beginning in 2026, fee free days at national parks will only be for U.S. residents. Non-U.S. residents will have to pay the entrance fee and nonresident fee as normal.

Página oficial NPS: Nonresident Fees — National Park Service
https://www.nps.gov/aboutus/nonresident-fees.htm

## Nonresident Fees

## What is a nonresident fee?
President Trump’s Executive Order Making America Beautiful Again by Improving Our National Parks directed the Secretary of Interior to develop “a strategy to increase revenue and improve the recreational experience at national parks by appropriately increasing entrance fees and recreation pass fees for nonresidents in areas of the National Park System that charge entrance fees.” The Executive Order directs that these fees be used “to improve the infrastructure of, or otherwise enhance enjoyment of or access to, America’s Federal recreational areas.” The Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture have created a nonresident fee that will be charged to each non-U.S. resident aged 16 and older that visits any of 11 of the most visited national parks: Acadia, Bryce Canyon, Everglades, Glacier, Grand Canyon, Grand Teton, Rocky Mountain, Sequoia & Kings Canyon, Yellowstone, Yosemite, and Zion. Non-U.S. residents will pay the standard entrance fee at each of these parks, plus a $100 fee per person aged 16 or older.

## How many people are covered by a nonresident fee?
Each non-U.S. resident aged 16 and over will be charged the $100 nonresident fee. This is a per-person fee.

Página oficial NPS: Entrance Passes — National Park Service
https://www.nps.gov/planyourvisit/passes.htm

## 2026 Free Entrance Days in the National Parks
Come experience the national parks! All National Park Service sites that charge an entrance fee will offer free admission to everyone (other fees, including timed entry or reservation fees, may apply). Mark your calendar for these entrance fee-free dates:
- February 16 : Presidents Day (Washington's Birthday)
- May 25 : Memorial Day
- June 14: Flag Day/President Trump's birthday
- July 3–5: Independence Day weekend
- August 25: 110th Birthday of the National Park Service
- September 17: Constitution Day
- October 27 : Theodore Roosevelt's birthday
- November 11: Veterans Day
Beginning in 2026, free entrance on these days will be for US citizens and residents only. Nonresidents will pay the regular entrance fee and any applicable nonresident fees.

## Your Fee Dollars at Work
All the money from entrance fees remains in the National Park Service, and at least 80 percent stays in the park where it was collected. Learn more about how entrance fees are used to improve the visitor experience .

### Overnight guest lodging closure in effect

## Phantom Ranch
Visit our Key Hiking Messages webpage for current trail closures near Phantom Ranch.
CLOSED — As of August 29, 2026, due to flash flooding:
The entirety of Phantom Ranch , including Bright Angel Campground , the Phantom Ranch Canteen , and Phantom Ranch cabins . The Black Bridge and Silver Bridge spanning the Colorado River.
The entirety of the North Kaibab Trail. This includes the North Kaibab Trailhead to Phantom Ranch . This closure is a result of significant flash flooding to the Bright Angel Canyon on 8/29.
There is no estimated reopening of these closure areas at this time.
Phantom Ranch, at the bottom of the Grand Canyon, is a popular destination for both hikers and mule riders. Overnight dormitories and cabins can be reserved and meals are available for purchase. Advance reservations for meals and lodging are required.
Phantom Ranch Reservations are made through Grand Canyon National Park Lodges (Xanterra Parks and Resorts) via an on-line lottery 15 months in advance.
( An NPS backcountry camping permit is not required for overnight stays in Phantom Ranch accomodations.) The park's Backcountry Information Center does not make reservations for Phantom Ranch lodging or meals. Reservations are made through Grand Canyon National Park Lodges.
Reservations for the nearby Bright Angel Campground (NPS) are made through the park's Backcountry Information Center.

## South Rim Shuttle Bus Service
Free shuttle buses operate year-round. Park you vehicle at, or near your lodge and let the buses take you around the village, out to scenic overlooks and trailheads.
When you arrive on the South Rim, you will receive a copy of the South Rim Pocket Map and Services Guide. The map below shows the lodges and their relation to this season's shuttle bus routes. You may download a copy of the map here .
Three shuttle bus routes are in service from September. 12, through November 30, 2026. Kaibab Rim (Orange) Route, right, travels to S. Kaibab Trailhead, outstanding scenic views at Yaki Point, and Yavapai Geology Museum. Village (Blue) Route, center, connects Visitor Center with lodges, campgrounds, Backcountry Information Center, and Market Plaza (general store and post office). Hermit Road (Red) Route travels a 7-mile scenic road with spectacular overlooks.
Visit this webpage (updated daily) for the South Rim list of what is open and closed, along with hours of operation.

Parque: Parque Nacional del Gran Cañón — Sección: accessibility

## Accesibilidad

- **Rim Trail** (South Rim, tramo pavimentado de ~20 km): plano y accesible en su mayoría, con múltiples miradores (Mather Point, Yavapai Point) directamente conectados.
- **Desert View Watchtower:** accesible por fuera; el interior de la torre tiene escaleras.
- El **shuttle gratuito del South Rim** tiene unidades accesibles para sillas de ruedas.
- Ningún sendero hacia el interior del cañón (Bright Angel, South Kaibab) es accesible — son empinados con terreno irregular.

## Nonresident Fees (cont.)

## How will NPS staff check residency status?
To purchase an America the Beautiful Resident Annual Pass, a visitor will need to show proof of U.S. citizenship or residency. Acceptable documents include a U.S. Passport, U.S. government (state or territory)-issued driver's license or state ID, or Permanent Resident card ("green card").

## How will residency be checked for purchasing digital passes?
Purchasers will show a photo ID at time of use (which is the current practice for all annual passes). If the purchaser is not eligible for the resident pass, they will be asked to upgrade to the non-resident pass. When checking out for the digital pass, language is included to ensure the purchaser understands eligibility and photo ID requirements.

## What is the price of the America the Beautiful Annual Pass?
The Departments of the Interior and Agriculture created a new pricing tier for the America the Beautiful Annual Pass starting January 1, 2026. U.S. residents will be able to purchase an annual pass for $80. Nonresidents will be able to purchase an annual pass for $250. The $250 pass covers the entire vehicle, or 2 motorcycles, or the passholder plus three additional adults in their party (where per-person rather than per-vehicle fees are charged).

## Nonresident Fees

## What is a nonresident fee?
President Trump’s Executive Order Making America Beautiful Again by Improving Our National Parks directed the Secretary of Interior to develop “a strategy to increase revenue and improve the recreational experience at national parks by appropriately increasing entrance fees and recreation pass fees for nonresidents in areas of the National Park System that charge entrance fees.” The Executive Order directs that these fees be used “to improve the infrastructure of, or otherwise enhance enjoyment of or access to, America’s Federal recreational areas.” The Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture have created a nonresident fee that will be charged to each non-U.S. resident aged 16 and older that visits any of 11 of the most visited national parks: Acadia, Bryce Canyon, Everglades, Glacier, Grand Canyon, Grand Teton, Rocky Mountain, Sequoia & Kings Canyon, Yellowstone, Yosemite, and Zion. Non-U.S. residents will pay the standard entrance fee at each of these parks, plus a $100 fee per person aged 16 or older.

## How many people are covered by a nonresident fee?
Each non-U.S. resident aged 16 and over will be charged the $100 nonresident fee. This is a per-person fee.

Regardless of the year issued, all valid America the Beautiful Passes and park-specific annual passes will cover entrance fees and nonresident fees for the pass holder and passengers in a private vehicle or on two motorcycles. At sites that charge per person, all valid America the Beautiful Passes and park-specific annual passes will cover entrance fees and nonresident fees for the pass holder and three additional adults.

## How will fee free days work?
Fee free days generally allow free entrance to all park visitors. Beginning in 2026, fee free days at national parks will only be for U.S. residents. Non-U.S. residents will have to pay the entrance fee and nonresident fee as normal.

Parque: Parque Nacional Joshua Tree — Sección: faqs

P: ¿Cuánto cuesta entrar?
R: 30 USD por vehículo, válido 7 días. Verifica en nps.gov/jotr.

P: ¿Necesito reservar para entrar?
R: No hay reservación de entrada requerida, pero los campamentos se reservan en recreation.gov. En temporada alta (octubre-mayo) se llenan rápido.

P: ¿Se puede ir en un día desde LA o San Diego?
R: Sí, es el parque estrella para escapadas de fin de semana desde SoCal: 2.5 h desde LA y 3 h desde San Diego. Puedes ver lo esencial en un día, pero una noche en camping vale mucho la pena.

P: ¿Cuándo es mejor ir?
R: De octubre a abril. El verano es extremadamente caliente (45°C+) y peligroso para caminar. La primavera (febrero-abril) tiene flores del desierto y es espectacular.

P: ¿Hay que llevar mucha agua?
R: Sí, más de lo que crees. El parque no tiene agua potable en la mayoría de las áreas; trae mínimo 4 litros por persona por día, aunque sea una visita corta.

P: ¿Es bueno para ver estrellas?
R: Sí, es uno de los mejores cielos nocturnos accesibles desde el sur de California. Sin luz artificial, el Milky Way se ve a simple vista.

P: ¿Se puede escalar?
R: Es uno de los destinos de escalada más famosos del mundo, pero para principiantes hay opciones de boulder fácil. Consulta en el centro de visitantes Oasis.

## Nonresident Fees

## What is a nonresident fee?
President Trump’s Executive Order Making America Beautiful Again by Improving Our National Parks directed the Secretary of Interior to develop “a strategy to increase revenue and improve the recreational experience at national parks by appropriately increasing entrance fees and recreation pass fees for nonresidents in areas of the National Park System that charge entrance fees.” The Executive Order directs that these fees be used “to improve the infrastructure of, or otherwise enhance enjoyment of or access to, America’s Federal recreational areas.” The Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture have created a nonresident fee that will be charged to each non-U.S. resident aged 16 and older that visits any of 11 of the most visited national parks: Acadia, Bryce Canyon, Everglades, Glacier, Grand Canyon, Grand Teton, Rocky Mountain, Sequoia & Kings Canyon, Yellowstone, Yosemite, and Zion. Non-U.S. residents will pay the standard entrance fee at each of these parks, plus a $100 fee per person aged 16 or older.

## How many people are covered by a nonresident fee?
Each non-U.S. resident aged 16 and over will be charged the $100 nonresident fee. This is a per-person fee.

### No reservation needed for entry, no timed entry
Grand Canyon National Park is a remarkable destination that draws in excess of 5 million visitors annually from around the globe. Accessible through three distinct entrances, to enhance your experience and minimize wait times, consider the following tips:

- An America the Beautiful Non-Resident Annual Pass is available for $250, which covers the entire vehicle, or 2 motorcycles, or the passholder plus three additional adults in their party where per-person rather than per-vehicle fees are charged. Página oficial NPS: Nonresident Fees — National Park Service
https://www.nps.gov/aboutus/nonresident-fees.htm

## Nonresident Fees

## What is a nonresident fee?
President Trump’s Executive Order Making America Beautiful Again by Improving Our National Parks directed the Secretary of Interior to develop “a strategy to increase revenue and improve the recreational experience at national parks by appropriately increasing entrance fees and recreation pass fees for nonresidents in areas of the National Park System that charge entrance fees.” The Executive Order directs that these fees be used “to improve the infrastructure of, or otherwise enhance enjoyment of or access to, America’s Federal recreational areas.” The Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture have created a nonresident fee that will be charged to each non-U.S. resident aged 16 and older that visits any of 11 of the most visited national parks: Acadia, Bryce Canyon, Everglades, Glacier, Grand Canyon, Grand Teton, Rocky Mountain, Sequoia & Kings Canyon, Yellowstone, Yosemite, and Zion. Non-U.S. residents will pay the standard entrance fee at each of these parks, plus a $100 fee per person aged 16 or older.

## How many people are covered by a nonresident fee?
Each non-U.S. resident aged 16 and over will be charged the $100 nonresident fee. This is a per-person fee.

Página oficial NPS: Nonresident Fees — National Park Service
https://www.nps.gov/aboutus/nonresident-fees.htm

## Nonresident Fees (cont.)

## How will NPS staff check residency status?
To purchase an America the Beautiful Resident Annual Pass, a visitor will need to show proof of U.S. citizenship or residency. Acceptable documents include a U.S. Passport, U.S. government (state or territory)-issued driver's license or state ID, or Permanent Resident card ("green card").

## How will residency be checked for purchasing digital passes?
Purchasers will show a photo ID at time of use (which is the current practice for all annual passes). If the purchaser is not eligible for the resident pass, they will be asked to upgrade to the non-resident pass. When checking out for the digital pass, language is included to ensure the purchaser understands eligibility and photo ID requirements.

## What is the price of the America the Beautiful Annual Pass?
The Departments of the Interior and Agriculture created a new pricing tier for the America the Beautiful Annual Pass starting January 1, 2026. U.S. residents will be able to purchase an annual pass for $80. Nonresidents will be able to purchase an annual pass for $250. The $250 pass covers the entire vehicle, or 2 motorcycles, or the passholder plus three additional adults in their party (where per-person rather than per-vehicle fees are charged).

Parque: Parque Nacional Death Valley — Sección: preparation

No necesitas condición física para Death Valley en invierno. Necesitas logística de desierto extremo.

Lo básico: ve de noviembre a marzo, sal temprano, tanque lleno, mucha agua y comida desde antes de entrar. Casi todas las paradas principales son planas o se ven desde el coche.

Si caminas (Golden Canyon, dunas): hazlo en la mañana o al final de la tarde, nunca a mediodía en calor. Lleva más agua de la que crees.

## Plan de Preparación
1. Temporada: noviembre a marzo. Evita el verano.
2. Tanque lleno y medio tanque como mínimo siempre; la gasolina adentro es cara y escasa.
3. Agua y comida compradas antes de entrar.
4. Mapas offline descargados (no hay señal).
5. Sombrero, bloqueador, lentes y zapato cerrado.
6. Sal temprano y dile a alguien tu ruta.
7. Empieza por Zabriskie Point al amanecer y Badwater; ve sumando.

Parque: Parque Nacional Death Valley — Sección: gear

**Lo esencial:**
- **Agua: 4+ litros (1 galón) por persona al día** — más en calor extremo
- Comida y snacks (los servicios adentro son pocos y caros)
- Sombrero de ala ancha, bloqueador y lentes de sol
- Tanque lleno de gasolina (la próxima gasolinera puede estar muy lejos)

**Opcional pero recomendado:**
- Hielera con agua extra en el coche
- Capa ligera para el frío de la mañana y la noche

Parque: Parque Nacional Death Valley — Sección: hikes

• Golden Canyon (4.8km, 2h), 90m desnivel — Este sendero ofrece una caminata colorida a través de cañones de arenisca, ideal para los aficionados a la geología. Apto principiante: sí
• Badwater Basin (1.6km, 1h), 0m desnivel — Camina sobre la salina al punto más bajo de Norteamérica (282 ft bajo el nivel del mar). Plano. Evita el calor del mediodía. Apto principiante: sí
• Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes (3km, 1.5h), 30m desnivel — Camina entre dunas; no hay sendero marcado. Ve temprano o al atardecer y lleva agua. Apto principiante: sí

Página oficial NPS: Hiking — Death Valley National Park
https://www.nps.gov/deva/planyourvisit/hiking.htm

## Hiking
Check Current Road Conditions
If you choose to travel on backcountry roads, be aware that rescue is likely to be extremely delayed. Travel prepared to survive, with 2 full size spare tires and extra food and water.
Current Road Conditions
There are few constructed trails here, but in a place this desolate you usually don't need them. Most hiking routes in the park are cross-country, up canyons, or along ridges.
Hiking Seasons
The best time to hike in Death Valley is from November through March. Summer temperatures can be dangerous in the park's lower elevations. Even during spring and autumn the heat can be unbearable for most people. Save the low elevation hikes for the cooler winter days. The high peaks are a pleasant escape from the heat in summer, but are usually covered with snow in the winter and spring. If you must climb them during winter season, be sure to be properly equipped with adequate winter clothing, an ice axe and crampons.
Water
Due to the dry climate of Death Valley, you must drink more water here than in other places, even in the cooler winter months. Always carry adequate water (at least 2 liters for a short winter dayhike, 1 gallon or more for longer warm season hikes and overnighters). Springs are rare and should not be considered reliable. Boil or treat water from these sources before using.

Parque: Parque Nacional Death Valley — Sección: safety

## Seguridad real (no para asustarte, para que regreses bien)

- **Agua — lo más crítico del país.** En verano el calor supera los 50°C. Lleva **4+ litros (1 galón) por persona al día**; más en calor extremo.
- **Gasolina.** Las distancias son enormes. Nunca dejes que el tanque baje de medio — carga en Furnace Creek.
- **Si el auto falla.** Quédate con el vehículo — es mucho más visible que tú. Nunca camines buscando ayuda.
- **Evita el verano.** De mayo a septiembre el parque puede ser letal para principiantes. Ve de noviembre a marzo.

Parque: Parque Nacional Death Valley — Sección: common_fears

P: ¿Es muy difícil para alguien sin experiencia?
R: No. El nombre asusta, pero casi todo se ve desde el auto o en caminatas cortas y planas. El reto no es físico, es el calor: con preparación, cualquiera lo visita.

P: ¿Qué hago si me encuentro con fauna peligrosa?
R: Coyotes y serpientes de cascabel viven aquí. Los coyotes te evitan; para serpientes, mira dónde pisas y dónde pones las manos. Nunca alimentes a nada. Ninguno te busca a ti.

P: ¿Puedo hacerlo en un solo día?
R: Sí. Badwater, Zabriskie Point y las dunas se ven en un día manejando entre paradas. Si vienes en invierno, alcanza de sobra para lo esencial sin correr.

P: ¿Y si me quedo sin gasolina o se descompone el auto?
R: Las distancias son largas y la gasolina escasea. Sal con tanque lleno, no dejes que baje de medio tanque y carga en Furnace Creek. Si el auto falla, quédate a la sombra del vehículo y espera: alguien pasará.

P: ¿Necesito caminar mucho o tener condición?
R: No. Casi todo se ve desde el auto o con caminatas cortas y planas (Badwater, Zabriskie, las dunas). No necesitas condición física, necesitas hidratarte y evitar el calor del mediodía.

P: ¿Hay agua adentro del parque?
R: Muy poca. Solo en Furnace Creek y un par de puntos. Lleva toda tu agua: al menos ~4 litros por persona al día, más en calor.

P: ¿Puedo ir en familia?
R: Sí, en invierno y con preparación. Las paradas son cortas y los paisajes impresionan a cualquier edad. Lleva agua de sobra, snacks y evita el verano por completo con niños.

Parque: Parque Nacional Death Valley — Sección: itinerary

Un día (invierno)

Llega temprano. Empieza en Zabriskie Point al amanecer (luz increíble, sin esfuerzo). Baja a Badwater Basin y camina un rato sobre la salina. Recorre Artists Drive. Por la tarde, las Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes con el sol bajando. Si quieres caminar más, la parte baja de Golden Canyon.

Dos días

Agrega Dante's View (vista enorme del valle) y, si el clima ayuda, más cañones. Quédate una noche en Furnace Creek o en un pueblo cercano para ver el cielo estrellado — es de los más oscuros del país.

Nota: en verano este itinerario NO es seguro a mediodía. Cámbialo a las primeras y últimas horas del día, o ve en invierno.

Página oficial NPS: Hiking — Death Valley National Park
https://www.nps.gov/deva/planyourvisit/hiking.htm

### Natural Bridge
Length: 1 mi (1.6 km) out and back round trip
Time: 45 minutes round trip
Difficulty: Easy
Elevation Gain: 86 ft (26m)
Location: The unpaved Natural Bridge Road is 13.5 miles (22km) south of CA-190 on Badwater Road and is typically passable to sedans.
Parking: Open parking area large enough for buses and RV's.
Closest Restroom: Vault toilet located in parking lot.
Route: The route from the information sign up the canyon to the bridge formation is easy to follow but very rocky. The canyon continues a short distance beyond the bridge where it abruptly ends at a dry waterfall.
Badwater Basin -the lowest place in North America.
NPS/K.Moses

### Badwater Salt Flat
Length: 1 mile (1.6km) out and back trip to edge of salt flat. 5 miles (8km) each way to the other side.

Parque: Parque Nacional Joshua Tree — Sección: gear

**Lo esencial:**

- **Agua: ~4 litros (1 galón) por persona al día** (más en verano)
- Sombrero de ala ancha, bloqueador solar y lentes de sol
- Zapato cerrado cómodo (*nada de sandalias*: hay rocas, cactus y serpientes)
- Una capa de abrigo para el frío de la tarde-noche
- **Linterna de cabeza (headlamp)** — ideal para ver estrellas
- Snacks salados y algo de comida
- **Mapa descargado offline** (app del NPS): no hay señal en el parque

**Opcional pero recomendado:**

- Bastones de trekking si subes Ryan Mountain
- Una cobija o silla para quedarte a ver las estrellas

Parque: Parque Nacional Joshua Tree — Sección: preparation

No necesitas ser atleta para Joshua Tree. Lo que necesitas es planear el calor y llevar suficiente agua.

## Plan de Preparación
1. Ve de octubre a abril — el verano supera los 38°C sin sombra.
2. Lleva mínimo 3-4 litros de agua por persona.
3. Llena el tanque antes de entrar — no hay gasolina dentro del parque.
4. Descarga el mapa offline; la señal es nula en la mayor parte del parque.
5. Empieza por Hidden Valley e Indian Cove — son los más accesibles para principiantes.

Parque: Parque Nacional Joshua Tree — Sección: safety

## Seguridad real (no para asustarte, para que regreses bien)

El desierto es manejable si lo respetas. Esto es lo que de verdad importa:

- **Agua — lo más importante.** Dentro del parque casi no hay. Lleva **mínimo 4 litros (1 galón) por persona al día**, más en verano. *No raciones de menos.* Llena tus botellas ANTES de entrar.
- **Calor.** En verano el sol de mediodía puede ser peligroso. Camina **temprano** y, si puedes, ve de **octubre a abril**.
- **Sin señal y sin sombra.** No hay señal de celular en casi todo el parque: **descarga el mapa offline** antes de entrar. Lleva sombrero, bloqueador y lentes.
- **No te salgas del sendero.** Las rocas se parecen entre sí y es fácil desorientarse. Quédate en el sendero marcado, **dile a alguien tu plan** y ponte una hora límite.
- **Serpientes de cascabel.** Camina viendo dónde pisas y **no metas manos ni pies en huecos de rocas**. Te evitan si no las sorprendes.
- **Lluvia e inundaciones.** Si llueve, *no entres a los cauces secos (washes)*: pueden crecer de golpe.

Parque: Parque Nacional Joshua Tree — Sección: faqs

P: ¿Cuánto cuesta entrar?
R: 30 USD por vehículo, válido 7 días. Verifica en nps.gov/jotr.

P: ¿Necesito reservar para entrar?
R: No hay reservación de entrada requerida, pero los campamentos se reservan en recreation.gov. En temporada alta (octubre-mayo) se llenan rápido.

P: ¿Se puede ir en un día desde LA o San Diego?
R: Sí, es el parque estrella para escapadas de fin de semana desde SoCal: 2.5 h desde LA y 3 h desde San Diego. Puedes ver lo esencial en un día, pero una noche en camping vale mucho la pena.

P: ¿Cuándo es mejor ir?
R: De octubre a abril. El verano es extremadamente caliente (45°C+) y peligroso para caminar. La primavera (febrero-abril) tiene flores del desierto y es espectacular.

P: ¿Hay que llevar mucha agua?
R: Sí, más de lo que crees. El parque no tiene agua potable en la mayoría de las áreas; trae mínimo 4 litros por persona por día, aunque sea una visita corta.

P: ¿Es bueno para ver estrellas?
R: Sí, es uno de los mejores cielos nocturnos accesibles desde el sur de California. Sin luz artificial, el Milky Way se ve a simple vista.

P: ¿Se puede escalar?
R: Es uno de los destinos de escalada más famosos del mundo, pero para principiantes hay opciones de boulder fácil. Consulta en el centro de visitantes Oasis.

Parque: Parque Nacional Joshua Tree — Sección: itinerary

## Medio día (principiante)

Entra por la **entrada oeste, temprano**. Camina el loop de **Hidden Valley** entre las rocas. Sigue con **Barker Dam** (loop fácil, a veces con agua y petroglifos). Pasa por Skull Rock o Cap Rock para fotos. Cierra con el **atardecer en Keys View**.

## Día completo

Agrega **Cholla Cactus Garden** (muy corto y plano; *no toques los cactus*). Si te queda energía y el clima ayuda, sube **Ryan Mountain** (exigente, las mejores vistas). Quédate a que oscurezca para ver el **cielo estrellado** — es de lo mejor del parque.

## Dos días

Duerme en un campground o en un motel del pueblo. Dedica el segundo día a la zona del **desierto de Colorado (sur)**: Cholla Cactus Garden y Ocotillo Patch, más tranquilos y con otro tipo de paisaje.

Página oficial NPS: Safety Guidelines for Your Visit to Joshua Tree National Park — Joshua Tree National Park
https://www.nps.gov/jotr/planyourvisit/safety-guidelines-for-your-visit-to-joshua-tree-national-park.htm

## Heat & Sun
Hazard : Desert temperatures can soar, leading to dehydration and heat illnesses. Temperatures can exceed 85°F (38°C) between April and September, with the hottest temperatures occurring in July and August. Some people are at higher risk of experiencing heat-illness.
Activities: Hiking, rock climbing, and outdoor exploring.
Safety Guidelines:
- Pick a “cool” activity at the park: Don’t let heat ruin your trip! Pick an activity that reduces your time in high temps. Consider doing a shorter hike, visiting the visitor center, or attending a ranger program to keep you and your travel companions cooler. Check out Oasis of Mara which has covered picnic area and water available.
- Stay hydrated: Carry at least a gallon of water per person each day. Keep a refillable water bottle and drink when thirsty. Here is a map of water stations in the park.
- Eat salty snacks: You need to take in calories to fuel your body. On a hot day, eating salty snacks can help your body replace electrolytes that are lost through sweating.
- Start your activity before 10 am or after 4 pm: Plan your activities during the cooler parts of the day (early morning or late evening).
- Watch for heat illness symptoms: Be aware of signs of heat exhaustion, such as dizziness, weakness, or excessive sweating. Take breaks in shaded areas, drink water, and rest frequently. If your symptoms get worse, seek immediate medical attention.

chunk_texts:
Página oficial NPS: Half Dome Day Hike — Yosemite National Park
https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/halfdome.htm

## Preparation (cont.)

### Water
One of the easiest ways to ensure a safe, enjoyable hike is to be sure to have plenty of water. Weather conditions and personal preference affect the amount of water you need, but suggested minimum amounts per person are:
1 gallon (4 liters) if hiking to the top of Half Dome
2 quarts (2 liters) if hiking only to the top of Nevada Fall
1 quart (1 liter) if hiking only to the top of Vernal Fall
The only treated water on the trail is available (summer only) at a drinking fountain at the Vernal Fall Footbridge (less than a mile from the trailhead). Merced River water is available up to Little Yosemite Valley, however you should treat this water by boiling, using iodine, or using a giardia-rated water filter. Drinking untreated river water may cause significant illness.

### Restrooms
Flush toilets are available at the Vernal Fall Footbridge (below Vernal Fall). Composting toilets are available near Emerald Pool (above Vernal Fall), near the top of Nevada Fall, and in Little Yosemite Valley.
At any other location, you are required to bury any solid human waste at least six inches (15 cm) deep and at least 100 feet (30 m) from water or trails. Pack out toilet paper.

Página oficial NPS: Half Dome Day Hike — Yosemite National Park
https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/halfdome.htm

## Introduction
Rising nearly 5,000 feet above Yosemite Valley and 8,800 feet above sea level, Half Dome is a Yosemite icon and a great challenge to many hikers. Despite an 1865 report declaring that it was "perfectly inaccessible, being probably the only one of the prominent points about the Yosemite which never has been, and never will be, trodden by human foot," George Anderson reached the summit in 1875, in the process laying the predecessor to today's cable route.
Today, thousands of people reach the summit. For most, it is an exciting, arduous hike; for a few, it becomes more of an adventure than they wanted. Indeed, park rangers assist hundreds of people on the Half Dome trail every summer. Most of these emergencies could have been prevented. Read on to learn how.
Much of the hike to Half Dome is an adventure into wilderness , and, while there is nothing you can do to guarantee your safety, below you will find some tips to reduce your risk and have a safer, more enjoyable hike.

Página oficial NPS: Half Dome Day Hike — Yosemite National Park
https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/halfdome.htm

## Hiking
The 14- to 16-mile round-trip hike to Half Dome is not for you if you're out of shape or unprepared. You will be gaining elevation (for a total of 4,800 feet) most of your way to the top of Half Dome. Most would say the reward is worth the effort. Along the way, you'll see outstanding views of Vernal and Nevada Falls, Liberty Cap, Half Dome, and—from the shoulder and summit—panoramic views of Yosemite Valley and the High Sierra.
Most hikers take 10 to 12 hours to hike to Half Dome and back; some take longer. If you plan on hiking during the day, it's smart to leave around sunrise (or earlier) and then have a non-negotiable turn-around time. For instance, if you haven't reached the top of Half Dome by 3:30 pm, you will turn around. Check for sunrise and sunset times before you hike. Regardless, each person should carry a good flashlight or headlamp with extra batteries (your cell phone doesn't count). Hikers commonly struggle down the trail after dark because they don't have a good light. Although the trail is well marked, you should be prepared with a good topographic map and compass and know how to use them.

Página oficial NPS: Half Dome Day Hike — Yosemite National Park
https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/halfdome.htm

## Safety

### Weather
The summit of Half Dome is a dangerous place during a lightning storm. Check the weather forecast before your hike and try to reach the summit early in the day to avoid thunderstorms, which are more common in the afternoon (but can occur at any time). If a storm appears nearby, do not continue to the summit and, if in the summit area, leave the area (while still using caution when descending the cables and steps).
The summit is typically 15°F (8°C) to 20°F (11°C) cooler than Yosemite Valley and windy conditions are common. Be prepared for cool temperatures and rain showers.
The leading cause of fatal falls from the cable route is being on the cables when the rock and/or cables are wet.

### Altitude Sickness
A few visitors each summer have problems with altitude sickness. Symptoms may include severe headache and/or nausea. The only way to relieve altitude sickness is to descend immediately. Other environmental illnesses include heat exhaustion, dehydration, and hyponatremia (low electrolyte levels). In addition to drinking plenty of water, be sure to eat salty snacks and to take regular rest breaks in the shade.

### Emerald Pool
Entering Emerald Pool and the Silver Apron is prohibited, and entering pools above waterfalls is strongly discouraged, because of frequent injuries and fatalities. Use extreme caution near flowing water; rocks adjacent to streams can be surprisingly slick.

Página oficial NPS: Half Dome Day Hike — Yosemite National Park
https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/halfdome.htm

## Safety (cont.)

## Trailhead and Parking Information
Most people begin the hike from Happy Isles (shuttle stop #16), which is about a half-mile from the trailhead parking lot or about 3/4 of a mile from Curry Village (parking available). Trailhead parking is just beyond Curry Village.
Shuttle service doesn't begin until 7 am, so if you're arriving prior to then, you can walk on the road (closed to all but authorized vehicles) from either parking area to the trailhead.
The nearest campgrounds are Upper, Lower, and North Pines Campgrounds , but reservations are very difficult to get in summer. Camp 4 may also be an option but also requires a reservation that can be hard to get.

## More Information
- Half Dome permits
- Campground reservations
- Camping without a reservation
- Half Dome Trail Stewardship Plan
Still have questions? Call a wilderness ranger at 209/372-0826 (Monday-Friday, 9 am to noon and 1 pm to 4:30 pm, from late May through early October).
Don't forget your camera and have a safe, enjoyable hike!

Parque: Parque Nacional Yosemite — Sección: common_fears

P: ¿Necesito ser montañista o estar en forma?
R: No para el Valle, que es plano y tiene shuttle. Las vistas más famosas están a corta caminata. La parte exigente (alto país, Half Dome) es opcional y para después. Para tu primera vez, quédate en el Valle.

P: ¿Qué hago si me encuentro con un oso?
R: Mantén la calma, haz ruido y retrocede lentamente sin darle la espalda.

P: ¿Es cierto que se necesita reservación para entrar?
R: En temporada alta, algunos años sí. Revisa las fechas en nps.gov antes de ir y, si aplica, reserva tu entrada con tiempo. Fuera de temporada alta no suele pedirse.

P: ¿Puedo subir Half Dome en mi primera visita?
R: Mejor no. Requiere permiso por lotería, se sube por cables sobre roca expuesta y ha habido accidentes mortales. No es una caminata para principiantes. Hay muchísimo que ver en el Valle sin ese riesgo.

P: Está lejos, ¿vale la pena el viaje?
R: Son 5 a 7 horas desde el sur de California, sí. Pero es uno de los parques más impresionantes del mundo y el Valle es fácil de disfrutar. Ve en primavera por las cascadas o en otoño por la calma y lo vas a recordar toda la vida.

Página oficial NPS: Half Dome Day Hike — Yosemite National Park
https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/halfdome.htm
